messages.subject: intercet-slope to loading-threshold
parts:
Dear Phil,
I hope you can help me with the following:
I try to get MIRT results comparable to those I get from MPlus. As far as I understand, I can get standardized loadings from summary() command and thresholds from coef(...,IRTpars=TRUE). Am I correct? I wanted to check whether I am getting what I want and therefore I have also manually recomputed slopes from coef() to loadings from summary() using the formula from Bock, et.al (as you reference to that paper in your MIRT jstatsoft paper). Well, I think I have the right formula, since it works for the example you have given in jstatsoft paper, i.e. for unidimensional model it is loading=slope/sqrt(1+slope^2). However, for the gpcm model with constrained loadings it does not work, at least not in my case:
coef(...,simplify=TRUE) gives me

messages.subject: Re: intercet-slope to loading-threshold
parts:
No definitely not, this requires changing from the c + aθ form to a(θ - b) form (which I have negative opinions about anyway), whereas the other transformation is into the standardized ogive metric, which is also slope-intercept. Check the code in mirt:::mirt2traditional for the correct transformation to the classical IRT form. 

Phil
